_comment: Right Path Daily Direction / Next Best Action decision. Adapted from IPF (bobpfromm/ipf-stewardship) src/rules/next-best-action.json, the established GoRules ZEN decision layer. ZEN owns ALL priority ordering: the composition passes only the independent presence of each kind of work and lets these ordered rows decide which wins. No priority is encoded in TypeScript. The ordering reflects only established Right Path distinctions and invents none: a promised callback that is DUE is due action work surfaced distinctly; ready-to-call and ready-to-email are both ordinary outreach action work with NO preference between them (the board groups them together and no business rule ranks calls over emails); research-needed is explicitly the exception path on the board, so it comes after ordinary action work; waiting states come last; an empty board is open capacity. A date-only callback is DUE WORK, not a fixed-time interruption, so it does not automatically outrank all other work.

rules._description: A customer we promised a callback that is now due is due action work and is surfaced first among action work (a kept commitment that has come due). Date-only: due work, not a fixed-time interruption.

Ordinary outreach action work: ready-to-call. Ready-to-call and ready-to-email are peers (no business rule ranks one above the other); when both are present either row matching first is immaterial because both resolve to ordinary outreach. Ready-to-call is listed first only so a single kind can be named, not as a preference.
Ordinary outreach action work: ready-to-email, when there is no ready-to-call work. Same tier as ready-to-call.
Research-needed is the explicit EXCEPTION path on the board, so it comes after ordinary outreach action work: it is the next action only when no ordinary outreach remains.
No action work, but items are waiting on customers or carriers: nothing to push right now, work is in flight.
